```{r}
#| include: false
# ============================================================
# SETUP: packages and raw data
# All data files live in the "data/" folder next to this qmd
# ============================================================
library(tidyverse)
library(gtsummary)

unemployment <- read.csv("data/unemployment_ls.csv")  # IMF Labor Statistics (LS), quarterly
aiax         <- read.csv("data/aiax.csv")             # IMF AI Adoption Index (AIAX), monthly
weo          <- read.csv("data/weo.csv")              # IMF World Economic Outlook (WEO), annual
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# ============================================================
# DATA PREP 1: unemployment rate (wide -> long, country-quarter)
# ============================================================

# Missingness check (for reference only, not shown in the PDF)
colSums(is.na(unemployment))
table(rowSums(is.na(unemployment[, 9:20])))

# Reshape quarterly columns (X2023.Q1 ... X2025.Q4) into rows
unemp_long <- unemployment %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 9:20, names_to = "quarter", values_to = "unemployment_rate") %>%
  mutate(
    iso3 = substr(SERIES_CODE, 1, 3),                 # ISO3 country code, e.g. "BRA"
    # "X2023.Q1": year = characters 2-5, quarter number = character 8
    year = as.integer(substr(quarter, 2, 5)),
    qtr  = as.integer(substr(quarter, 8, 8))
  )
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# ============================================================
# DATA PREP 2: AI Adoption Index (monthly -> quarterly)
# Keep the three country-level monthly indicators and put each in its own column
# ============================================================
aiax_q <- aiax %>%
  filter(FREQUENCY == "Monthly") %>%
  mutate(
    iso3 = sub("\\..*", "", SERIES_CODE),             # everything before the first "."
    ai_var = case_when(
      INDICATOR == "Share of Emerging AI" ~ "ai_share",
      grepl("low-exposure",  INDICATOR, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "ai_share_low_exp",
      grepl("high-exposure", INDICATOR, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "ai_share_high_exp"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(iso3, ai_var, matches("^X\\d{4}\\.M\\d{2}$")) %>%   # monthly columns only
  pivot_longer(-c(iso3, ai_var), names_to = "month_label", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    # "X2023.M01": year = characters 2-5, month = characters 8-9
    year  = as.integer(substr(month_label, 2, 5)),
    month = as.integer(substr(month_label, 8, 9)),
    qtr   = ceiling(month / 3)                        # months 1-3 -> Q1, etc.
  ) %>%
  group_by(iso3, ai_var, year, qtr) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ai_var, values_from = value) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ai_share))                            # drop quarters with no overall AI data
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# ============================================================
# DATA PREP 3: WEO macro variables (one row per country-year)
# ============================================================
weo_clean <- weo %>%
  mutate(
    iso3 = sub("\\..*", "", SERIES_CODE),             # everything before the first "."
    indicator = case_when(
      grepl("NGDP_RPCH", SERIES_CODE) ~ "gdp_growth",       # real GDP growth (%)
      grepl("PCPIPCH",   SERIES_CODE) ~ "inflation",        # CPI inflation, period average (%)
      grepl("NGDPDPC",   SERIES_CODE) ~ "gdp_per_capita"    # GDP per capita, current USD
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(iso3, indicator, starts_with("X")) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("X"), names_to = "year", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(substr(year, 2, 5))) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = indicator, values_from = value)

# IMF WEO advanced economies (ISO3 codes)
# NOTE: verify against the current WEO country classification before final use
advanced_iso3 <- c(
  "AND", "AUS", "AUT", "BEL", "CAN", "HRV", "CYP", "CZE", "DNK", "EST",
  "FIN", "FRA", "DEU", "GRC", "HKG", "ISL", "IRL", "ISR", "ITA", "JPN",
  "KOR", "LVA", "LTU", "LUX", "MAC", "MLT", "NLD", "NZL", "NOR", "PRT",
  "PRI", "SMR", "SGP", "SVK", "SVN", "ESP", "SWE", "CHE", "TWN", "GBR",
  "USA"
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# ============================================================
# DATA PREP 4: merge into the analysis dataset (country-quarter)
# ============================================================
analysis_df <- unemp_long %>%
  dplyr::select(iso3, COUNTRY, year, qtr, unemployment_rate) %>%
  filter(!is.na(unemployment_rate)) %>%
  inner_join(aiax_q, by = c("iso3", "year", "qtr")) %>%   # keep country-quarters in both
  left_join(weo_clean, by = c("iso3", "year")) %>%        # add annual macro variables
  mutate(
    economy_group = if_else(iso3 %in% advanced_iso3,
                            "Advanced", "Emerging/Developing"),
    qtr = factor(qtr)                                     # quarter as categorical (seasonality)
  )

# Quick checks (not shown in the PDF)
nrow(analysis_df)                    # expected: 826
n_distinct(analysis_df$iso3)         # expected: 82
analysis_df %>% count(economy_group)

# Countries behind extreme values
analysis_df %>% filter(ai_share > 5) %>% distinct(COUNTRY, economy_group)
analysis_df %>% filter(unemployment_rate > 20) %>% distinct(COUNTRY)
```

```{r}
# Snapshot of the analysis dataset (one row per country-quarter)
glimpse(analysis_df)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 6
# Histogram of the outcome in the analytic sample
ggplot(analysis_df, aes(x = unemployment_rate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Quarterly Unemployment Rates, 2023-2025",
    x = "Unemployment rate (%)",
    y = "Number of country-quarters"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 6
# Key relationship on log scales (both variables are right-skewed)
# log1p = log(1 + x), which handles AI shares equal to 0
# Separate fitted lines by economy group preview the planned interaction
ggplot(analysis_df, aes(x = ai_share, y = unemployment_rate, color = economy_group)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log1p", breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "AI Adoption in Job Postings and Unemployment Rate",
    x = "Share of job postings requiring emerging AI skills (log scale)",
    y = "Unemployment rate (%, log scale)",
    color = "Economy group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Table 1: descriptive statistics by economy group
analysis_df %>%
  dplyr::select(unemployment_rate, ai_share, ai_share_high_exp, ai_share_low_exp,
                gdp_growth, inflation, gdp_per_capita, economy_group) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = economy_group,
    statistic = all_continuous() ~ "{median} ({p25}, {p75})",
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 2,
    label = list(
      unemployment_rate ~ "Unemployment rate (%)",
      ai_share          ~ "AI share, all occupations",
      ai_share_high_exp ~ "AI share, high-exposure occupations",
      ai_share_low_exp  ~ "AI share, low-exposure occupations",
      gdp_growth        ~ "Real GDP growth (%)",
      inflation         ~ "Inflation (%)",
      gdp_per_capita    ~ "GDP per capita (USD)"
    ),
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  as_kable(caption = "Table 1. Median (IQR) of key variables by economy group")
```

**Outcome.** The analytic sample contains 826 country-quarter observations from 82 economies (403 from advanced economies and 423 from emerging/developing economies) between 2023 and 2025. The median quarterly unemployment rate is 5.17% (IQR: 3.60–7.39%). The distribution is right-skewed, with a small number of observations above 20% from South Africa and Botswana, two economies with well-documented structural unemployment. We retain these observations and will consider a log transformation of the outcome.

**Key relationship.** The share of job postings requiring emerging AI skills is also highly right-skewed: most observations are below 2%, while a few smaller economies (e.g., Cyprus, Slovenia, Latvia, Bolivia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia) exceed 5%. Because these economies have relatively small online job-posting markets, their high values may partly reflect measurement noise. We will assess the sensitivity of our results to these observations.

**Covariates.** Advanced economies have more than twice the median AI share of emerging/developing economies (0.22% vs. 0.09%), but they also differ systematically in GDP growth, inflation, and GDP per capita (Table 1). This highlights the need to adjust for these macroeconomic variables as potential confounders.
